item.content:encoded:
It’s not supposed to be linezolid or any other real oxazolidinone antibiotic. It is supposed to be a fictional antibiotic in the same family, produced by an anomalous yeast. It was extraordinarily powerful and *unlike* actual oxazolidinone antibiotics such as linezolid, devoid of substantial side effects. In universe the chemical was identified and a mundane chemical synthesis devised, making it an -EX

Edit: one comment, as others have noted, there is actually zero technobabble here. This is written pretty much exactly the way a brief semi-technical overview document describing the same thing would be written in real life for a government research agency. I can easily imagine this as the “abstract” for the whole file describing details of discovery, activity spectrum, structural ID and development of the mundane synthesis.

Honestly, I can see where you're coming from, but I'm gonna have to disagree.

"SCP-4023-EX is a chemical compound currently marketed as the antibiotic █████████" is pretty darn straightforward. The rest could be just as easily followed if I redacted words like "oxazolidinone". Consider:

"SCP-4023-EX is a chemical compound currently marketed as the antibiotic [REDACTED]. It is a [REDACTED] antibiotic agent capable of killing nearly any naturally occurring [REDACTED] bacteria, but lacking the toxicity present in previously documented [REDACTED] compounds. Structural details, mechanism of action, and production information are publicly available in several peer-reviewed scientific journals and on Wikipedia."

Redacting that stuff would be clumsy, but my basic premise here was to write it so that someone who didn't know a term could still read it.

item.content:encoded:
The researchers at first didn't know what it did or how to recreate it. If you were the researcher who was “saturated” by the chemical, your first reaction would probably be “OH SHIT I'M GOING TO DIE” depending on the SCP instead of “Hmm, I'm goopy or injected with this stuff or inhaled it or whatever. I wonder if it's an antibiotic.” The reason it became a -EX was because they didn't need the mystery SCP and its mysterious yeast anymore to synthesize the compound (after they figured out what it did). They were able to create it using known chemical compounds and practices.
For example, if the Foundation figured out how to reliably make Telekill or SCP-500 with what they know (instead of dumping ingredients into a blackbox machine like SCP-914) and “commonly” available materials, then they would become -EXes.
